ObjectName.value: Aerial Sunset Over Paranal

ImageDescription.value:
This remarkable image was taken using a quadcopter, hovering high above the Atacama. Ocean, cloud and desert come together to form the aerial scene, stretching out along the Chilean coast.

ESO’s Very Large Telescope (VLT) is softly illuminated by the Sun as it sets in the evening sky, throwing hues of orange and apricot across the observatory. On an adjacent peak towards the right of the frame, the 4.1-metre Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy (VISTA) stands apart, cutting a more solitary figure.

The region in front of the VLT, filled with a lattice-like grid of rails, is used by the four small movable VLT Auxiliary Telescopes. Placing these telescopes at different distances apart adjusts the effective size of the VLT Interferometer, which acts as a single giant stargazer.

ObjectName.value: Líneas de Nazca, Nazca, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 49

ImageDescription.value: Aerial view of the "Monkey", one of the most popular geoglyphs of the Nazca Lines, which are located in the Nazca Desert in southern Peru. The geoglyphs of this UNESCO World Heritage Site (since 1994) are spread over a 80 km (50 mi) plateau between the towns of Nazca and Palpa and are, according to some studies, between 500 B.C. and 500 A.D. old.

Both areas retain the hues characteristic of late summertime, with deep green trees hovering over medium green fields. ObjectName.value: Sta. Cruz Sand Bar

ImageDescription.value: Aerial Panorama shot of Sta. Cruz Island Sand Bar, Zamboanga City. Tucked away on the coast of the Philippines lies Zamboanga City, home, to a treasure that captivates the hearts of all who visit. The Sta. Cruz Island Sandbar. This enchanting destination has gained popularity among travelers seeking a beach experience thanks to its one of a kind sands and mesmerizing natural beauty. What makes Sta. Cruz Island unique is its shoreline adorned with rosy hued sand a result of tiny organisms called Foraminifera. These minuscule creatures boast shells made of calcium carbonate, which gradually blend with the white sand and create a breathtaking palette of pink shades, along the coast. Recognizing the importance of preserving Sta. Cruz Islands natural wonder local authorities have taken steps to protect its ecosystem by designating it as a protected area. This conservation effort not safeguards the islands charm but also ensures that future generations can revel in its magical allure.

Artist.value: Aldous Mariano Cariño
